name: Swamp Green
lede: Swamp Green is a plain descriptive name for a murky, yellowish olive green; as a listed color it is recent, and the books treat it only as a dictionary entry.

sections.title: A descriptive name
sections.body:
Paterson's dictionary defines swamp green simply as a dark, murky green, and lists it among the greens in its color index [1]. It has no pigment or dye behind it and no known coiner. The books name no maker, date or story for it, so its origin is undocumented.

In our library the name comes from the xkcd color survey of 2010, which is the earliest record we hold [2]. The swatch here is a fairly saturated olive; its nearest named neighbor is [[olive]], 4.6 units away on the CIEDE2000 scale [2]. That is brighter and yellower than Paterson's word "murky" suggests [1][2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our archive, a color near Swamp Green appears in 18 of 23,781 paintings, or 0.08 per cent, and it is rarer than 68 per cent of the named colors [3]. Where it does appear it is usually an accent, in 9 of the 10 paintings that give a within-painting reading, and it peaks in the 1800s [3]. The earliest match is dated 1801, 209 years before the name's first record, so it is a look-alike hue in an aged photograph and not evidence of any pigment [3].

Swamp Green is a historic pigment with a documented maker.
